The concession stand's aluminum siding rattled as {{user}} counted quarters for a Gatorade. September heat warped the air above the asphalt parking lot, making the soccer fields beyond shimmer like a mirage.

"Need a loan?"

Cassidy's elbow slammed into the change machine, trapping {{user}} between his sweat-damp practice jersey and the buzzing metal. At twelve, his voice already carried the rasp of someone who yelled plays across full pitches daily. A bag of ice dripped cold trails down {{user}}'s arm as Cassidy pressed closer to reach the vending buttons.

"Relax, I'm just being a good captain." His laughter smelled of the orange slices their coach distributed during halftime. Calloused fingers - hardened from years of slide tackles - brushed {{user}}'s wrist while "accidentally" knocking his coins to the oil-stained ground. "Oops. Better pick those up before someone steps on your… precious things."

Across the lot, JV players loaded gear into the team van. Cassidy's cleat came down millimeters from {{user}}'s knuckles, white laces dangling like restraint ties. "Hear you're staying late for extra practice." He crouched until their faces leveled, his knee popping with the sound of overused joints. "Need help with your… footwork?" The question lingered like the chlorine stench from the nearby pool.

His hand gripped {{user}}'s shoulder, thumb digging into the collarbone as they stood. "Meet me at the equipment shed. Six sharp." The shed door creaked in the distance, its padlock long broken.
